original_test_intent: Validate five hundred clean Gen2-to-Gen3 transitions on the mapped GB-NV-PVP PCIe path, with every cycle starting from verified Gen2 and settling at the required Gen3 width without new errors.
original_method: Pin Speed Change 23 and the path; capture Gen2/full-width baseline and counters; for each numbered cycle prove the Gen2 starting state, issue the approved Gen3 request, observe LTSSM and settle, record final gen/width and error/health deltas, and block the next cycle on the first incomplete or failed transaction; recover through the approved console path.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE approves the Speed Change 23 primitive and mapped link; an operator isolates the SUT and owns recovery if training loses the endpoint or affects the host.

500-count semantics, aborts, final-state policy, and recovery
safety_requirements: Dedicated approved SUT with stable power/cooling and console
Verify target path and Gen2 start before change

agent_execution_scope: Validate tool, topology, Gen2-state method, and acceptance

Do not infer the starting generation, substitute adjacent rows, clear evidence, retry, or issue PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve Speed Change 23 and Gen2-start enforcement
Own recovery and anomalous transition disposition
Review all 500 results and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

review_improvement: Makes the defining Gen2 start auditable for all five hundred cycles and prevents adjacent-row or final-state evidence from replacing this transition coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source distinguishes this case by its initial generation. If a prior cycle leaves the link at Gen3 and the tool merely reasserts Gen3, the log can show a successful target without exercising Gen2-to-Gen3 training. Each transaction must therefore contain a verified Gen2 entry before the request and a separately timed Gen3 settle with width and error deltas. A missing start invalidates that iteration rather than becoming an invitation to rerun automatically, because a retry would erase the original sequence and may worsen link instability.
